# SK1015 — Use `is T t` instead of `is T` and a cast

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A type test whose block opens by casting the same expression to the same type is one pattern.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 7.0 |
| Since | 1.2 |
| ReSharper | `MergeCastWithTypeCheck` (`resharper_merge_cast_with_type_check_highlighting`) |
| Supersedes | IDE0020 |

## Why

`if (x is Widget) { var w = (Widget)x; … }` tests the type and then converts it again, and the second conversion cannot fail — the compiler emits an `isinst` and a `castclass` where one `isinst` would do. A declaration pattern is the same program with one type check, and it makes the relationship between the test and the variable something the reader no longer has to reconstruct.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (node is BinaryExpressionSyntax) {
    var binary = (BinaryExpressionSyntax)node;
    Visit(binary.Left);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (node is BinaryExpressionSyntax binary) {
    Visit(binary.Left);
}
```

## When it does not fire

None known. It requires the cast to be the initializer of the block's *first* statement — the shape where the declaration already exists, so the fix moves one rather than inventing one — and requires the cast and the test to name the same type by symbol rather than by spelling, since `is IList` beside `(IList<int>)` share a prefix and can succeed and fail independently. An explicitly typed declaration is admitted only where its type is the tested type exactly, because a pattern variable is bound to the tested type and `object o = (Widget)x;` would not survive. It is silent on an `if` with an `else`, where the pattern variable is in scope but not definitely assigned; where lifting the name into the enclosing block would collide with another local scope of the member; and inside an expression tree, where a pattern is CS8122.
